positive.intent: Immediate throw can replace a pending exception; syntax is not proof of reachability.

negative.intent: Rethrow is in catch, not finally; cleanup itself has no throw.

suppression.intent: Genuine upstream file annotation on an otherwise identical, independently named package; neighboring original file must retain every positive finding. No ktChecker-ID or declaration-scope suppression claim.

controls.intent: Registering a deferred callback does not throw during finally. Preserve the descendant-only finding if observed.
The throw is caught entirely inside finally and does not discard an outer exception. Preserve the syntax alert rather than infer propagated failure.

limitations: All descendant throw expressions are visited, including deferred lambdas and locally handled throws; no control-flow or effect proof.
Advisory only; intentional exception replacement and reachability require owner/project context.

six_case_plan.positive: Run the exact selected route on positive immutable snapshot bytes.
six_case_plan.negative: Run legal alternative bytes with the same route still active.
six_case_plan.configuration: Run the original positive bytes with the owner-selected rule disabled; separately replay genuine options below when applicable.
six_case_plan.version: Replay positive bytes under the pinned CLI, retain actual CLI version output, and verify Common/Native requests never reach the runner. Declared Kotlin2.4.21/embedded2.4.10 stays unqualified.
six_case_plan.suppression: Use actual file-scoped upstream annotation with an unsuppressed neighboring file; never suppress/filter in host code.
six_case_plan.regression: Seal the negative correction as a child of the suppression snapshot, delete obsolete files, and verify both registered parent and child materializations.

qualification_note: Authored expected results are not observed behavior. Actual assertions, immutable materialization checks, raw SARIF/process receipts and START witnesses are required before a sidecar is emitted; no compatibility/precision/performance/release qualification is proposed.
